meta.description: Search NCBI databases using Biopython Bio.Entrez (ESearch, EInfo, EGQuery, ESpell). Use when finding records by keyword, building reproducible field-qualified queries, navigating the Entrez Query Translator, exploiting the history server for large result sets, handling retmax caps, or interpreting weekly index lag. Covers PubMed, Nucleotide, Protein, Gene, SRA, GEO, Assembly, Taxonomy, ClinVar, dbSNP.

scientific_integrity.detail: All counts, UIDs, and translations across all 6 executed inputs came from live NCBI E-utilities calls; none were fabricated. No DOI/PMID/p-value/sample-size claims were invented.

practice_boundaries.detail: Pure literature/database search tooling; no output makes diagnostic, prescriptive, or treatment claims about an individual. Not applicable to this Skill's scope.

methodological_ground.detail: No correlation/causation conflation or statistical fallacy in any output; the Skill's own guidance (evidence-hierarchy-adjacent EGQuery/ESearch distinction, index-lag caveats) was applied correctly where relevant.

code_usability.detail: All 6 executed scripts ultimately ran to completion with real, checked output. 2 of 6 (Inputs 2, 6) hit confirmed API-surface defects in the Skill's own documented code patterns (see recommendations), but both are one-line-fix field/attribute mismatches, not syntax errors, infinite loops, or missing dependencies -- the Skill's own 'Version Compatibility' instruction anticipates exactly this class of drift.

functional_suitability.note: Broad, accurate coverage of ESearch/EInfo/EGQuery/ESpell/history-server/retmax, but two of the Skill's own copy-pasteable code patterns (EGQuery call; EInfo DbInfo indexing) crash as written on the installed Biopython 1.88 -- confirmed by direct execution.

reliability.note: Failure Modes and Common Errors tables are unusually thorough and every entry spot-checked (retmax cap, WebEnv expiration, rate limits) matched live behavior exactly.

performance_context.note: Single flat ~300-line SKILL.md with no references/ split; examples/ exist but are never linked from SKILL.md or usage-guide.md.

agent_usability.note: Decision table plus Goal/Approach/Reference code-pattern structure is clear and consistent; a couple of patterns (e.g. list_fields) omit expected sample output.

human_usability.note: Natural trigger language in the description; usage-guide worked examples cover ambiguity/typos well, though one (MARCH1) has data-drifted -- see Input 4.

security.note: No credential-exposure risk in practice, but Required Setup hardcodes Entrez.api_key = 'YOUR_KEY' rather than an env-var pattern, and gives no input-validation guidance for term strings.

maintainability.note: Small, reusable functions per pattern, but no references/ modularity split despite non-trivial length.

agent_specific.note: Precise, well-calibrated trigger description and explicit Related Skills composability; missing progressive-disclosure split (references/) is the main gap.

key_strengths: Failure Modes and Common Errors tables are unusually thorough; every entry spot-checked (retmax cap, WebEnv-expiration semantics, rate-limit math) matched real, live NCBI behavior exactly.
History-server chaining/intersection is documented precisely and the multi-part chained-intersection pattern ran correctly end-to-end with real, sanity-checked counts (Input 5).

Explicit Related Skills cross-references correctly kept the agent in-scope: on the one out-of-scope request tested (Input 7), the Skill's own framing ('ESearch returns UIDs, not records') led to a correct redirect to entrez-fetch instead of fabricated content.
Rate-limit guidance (0.34s/0.10s, history-server-over-parallelism) is accurate and was applied consistently across every executed script.

recommendations.title: EGQuery documented as a core utility but nonexistent on Biopython 1.88
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md's decision table and usage-guide.md's 'Cross-database discovery' worked example both route through Entrez.egquery(), which raises AttributeError on the installed Biopython 1.88 -- the entire EGQuery code path, including examples/global_query.py's only top-level call, is unusable as shipped.
recommendations.root_cause: SKILL.md's reference code was written/tested against a Biopython version where Bio.Entrez.egquery existed; the function's removal from the installed 1.88 public API was never re-verified against.
recommendations.fix: Promote the already-correct ESearch-loop-over-CURATED_DBS fallback (examples/global_query.py) to the primary documented path, or add a version-pinned note flagging Bio.Entrez.egquery as broken on Biopython >=1.85 with a direct pointer to the fallback.

recommendations.title: EInfo DbInfo indexed as a dict in SKILL.md and examples/database_info.py, but Biopython 1.88 returns a list-of-one
recommendations.problem: Both SKILL.md's list_fields() (r['DbInfo']['FieldList']) and examples/database_info.py's db_info() (info['DbName']) raise TypeError: list indices must be integers or slices, not str on the installed Biopython version -- every EInfo code pattern in the Skill fails as written.
recommendations.root_cause: Biopython 1.88 wraps DbInfo as a one-element list; the return-shape change was never re-verified against the Skill's reference code.
recommendations.fix: Change both patterns to index r['DbInfo'][0], and add a one-line comment noting the list-of-one wrapping. Confirmed working after this one-line fix in this audit's Input 2.

recommendations.title: No progressive disclosure despite non-trivial SKILL.md length
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md is roughly 300 lines with all failure-modes, field tables, and code patterns inline; examples/ exists but is never referenced or linked from SKILL.md or usage-guide.md.
recommendations.root_cause: The Skill was authored as a single flat file without a references/ split or explicit examples/ cross-links.
recommendations.fix: Split the field-qualified-pattern tables and Failure Modes table into a references/ file, and add explicit 'See examples/basic_search.py' pointers next to the matching code patterns in SKILL.md.

recommendations.title: API key documented as a hardcoded placeholder, not an env-var pattern
recommendations.problem: 'Required Setup' shows Entrez.api_key = 'YOUR_KEY' as a literal assignment with no guidance to source it from an environment variable or secrets store.
recommendations.root_cause: The setup snippet was optimized for copy-paste clarity over credential hygiene.
recommendations.fix: Change the example to Entrez.api_key = os.environ.get('NCBI_API_KEY') and add one line warning never to commit a real key.

recommendations.title: MARCH1 worked example premise ('no hits') no longer reproduces against live data
recommendations.problem: usage-guide.md's 'Diagnosing a wrong count bug' prompt claims the original MARCH1 query returns zero hits; live testing today (gene db) returns 702 hits via the [All Fields] fallback, not zero -- the diagnostic technique still works but the narrative premise is stale.
recommendations.root_cause: NCBI's Entrez Query Translator / indexed content for this term has drifted since the example was authored; the example was never revisited.
recommendations.fix: Regenerate the worked example against a currently-reproducible ambiguous symbol, or soften the prompt to 'returned surprisingly broad/ambiguous hits' rather than a hard 'no hits' claim.
